item.title: orgstar 0.8.0
item.description:
Missed habits join the Overdue group, and the iPhone and iPad app gets an entry sheet, a first-launch guide and an About screen.

  • Overdue. A habit scheduled on an earlier day and not done goes in today's Overdue group, and every overdue row shows how late it is (2d ago) instead of the time of day it had.
  • iOS: entry sheet. Tapping an agenda entry opens a sheet to change its title, TODO state, priority, scheduled date, deadline, tags and notes, with undo and redo. Done writes the changes to the file together.
  • iOS: Overdue section. Overdue entries are a section of their own above today.
  • iOS: first launch. A few screens introduce the app, ask for the folder of org files, and offer notifications, Calendar events and Reminders, each asked for only when you choose it.
  • iOS: About. Settings ends with About orgstar: the version, the manual, release notes, the issue tracker, support email and the privacy policy.

Universal (Apple silicon and Intel), macOS 26 or later. Notarized.

item.title: orgstar 0.7.0
item.description:
Hide folders from the agenda, by hand or with a Focus, and agenda fixes.

  • Hiding folders. With more than one folder, the Folders menu in the agenda's toolbar shows or hides each folder's files in the agenda and the widgets; the shown folders' names appear under the title. Reminders still fire for hidden folders.
  • Focus filter. Add orgstar's Hide Folders filter to a Focus in System Settings ▸ Focus to hide its folders while the Focus is on and mute their reminders.
  • Archived tasks. agenda-exclude-archives in config.toml leaves out the files your agenda files archive to, by #+ARCHIVE:, an :ARCHIVE: property or org-archive-location.
  • Reminders. Notification titles are the heading without its TODO keyword and priority.
  • Fix. After a file changed, agenda rows could show another entry's title while opening the right one.

Universal (Apple silicon and Intel), macOS 26 or later. Notarized.

item.title: orgstar 0.6.1
item.description:
New star icons, and app icons that keep their colors in dark mode.

  • Star icons. The three unicorn icons are now Org Star, Night Star and Pastel Star: a full-size heading star on the same backgrounds. An icon chosen before stays chosen.
  • Dark mode. In the system's Dark icon style and in the Dock in dark appearance, each icon keeps a darkened version of its own colors instead of turning into the same glyph on gray.

Universal (Apple silicon and Intel), macOS 26 or later. Notarized.

item.title: orgstar 0.6.0
item.description:
Built-in themes and app icons.

  • Themes. Settings ▸ Appearance ▸ Theme chooses a theme for the light appearance and one for the dark: Default, Solarized, Gruvbox, Modus, Catppuccin, Tomorrow and Paper for light; Default, Solarized, Gruvbox, Modus, Catppuccin, Nord, Dracula, Tokyo Night and doom-one for dark. They are light-theme and dark-theme in config.toml, and colors set there or in a theme file still apply on top. Themes other than Default also color the sidebar, the modeline, the agenda and buttons.
  • Your own theme. Copy to Config Folder writes the two chosen themes into my-theme.toml, every color written out, to start from.
  • App icons. Settings ▸ Appearance ▸ App Icon offers thirteen icons, three of them unicorns, shown in the Dock while orgstar runs. The default icon follows the system's Default, Dark and Tinted icon styles.

Universal (Apple silicon and Intel), macOS 26 or later. Notarized.

item.title: orgstar 0.5.0
item.description:
Writing, search and export, Org's defaults, and a German translation of what's new.

  • Writing. A proportional body font (Settings ▸ Appearance ▸ Body text), with tables, code, dates and tags kept monospaced. A text width that centres lines in a wide window. Line numbers are off by default. Emphasize (C-c C-x C-f), with ⌘B, ⌘I and ⌘U in the Mac keys. The word count shows characters and reading time.
  • Search. Search Notes finds text before a file's first heading, and shows the passage each result matched with the words in bold.
  • Notes. Find Node and Insert Node Link make a new node from a title that isn't found. Backlinks show the line each link is on.
  • Export. Word files have heading styles and the file's images. PDF export has page numbers, and settings for margins and font in the Export dialog.
  • Safety. Recovery Versions keeps an hourly snapshot of a file before saving.
  • Org's defaults. New installs get Org's TODO keywords (TODO and DONE) and M-RET at the caret; existing settings are kept. Logging, speed keys and spell checking are in Settings ▸ Editing.
  • Getting started. A welcome sheet offers to add a folder or make one in iCloud Drive, and to choose the keys.
  • Smaller changes. The date prompt reads today, tomorrow, yesterday, next week and last week. Remove Schedule and Remove Deadline have keys. Recovery Versions, Resolve Sync Conflicts, Revert to File on Disk and Check Spelling While Typing are in the menus.

Universal (Apple silicon and Intel), macOS 26 or later. Notarized.

item.title: orgstar 0.4.2
item.description:
A fix for windows with several panes.

  • ⌘W or the × on a pane's only tab closes the pane instead of leaving it empty, and closes the buffer only when no other pane shows it. ⌘W on an empty pane closes the pane, not the window.

Universal (Apple silicon and Intel), macOS 26 or later. Notarized.

item.title: orgstar 0.4.1
item.description:
Fixes in the editor and in Word export.

  • M-RET at the end of a folded heading inserts the new heading after the subtree, as Emacs does with point behind the ellipsis, instead of between the heading and its hidden body.
  • Tabs stop every 8 columns from the start of the line, as in Emacs.
  • Word export sets a page size, Letter or A4 by region as PDF export does. Quick Look and Pages laid the document out on a narrow page without one.
  • iOS: the Schedule and Deadline prompts take a time; arrow keys skip folded text instead of opening it.

Universal (Apple silicon and Intel), macOS 26 or later. Notarized.

item.title: orgstar 0.4.0
item.description:
Images and files can be pasted and dropped into notes.

  • An image on the clipboard is saved as org-yank-image-save-method says and linked on a line of its own at the caret. Pasted or dropped files are handled as org-yank-dnd-method says. With the caret on an image line, the link shows with the image under it.
  • iOS: paste, drop and Take Photo in the editor; Attach Photo or Video inserts the link at the caret; Export Subtree… in the Export menu.

Universal (Apple silicon and Intel), macOS 26 or later. Notarized.

item.title: orgstar 0.3.2
item.description:
• Settings ▸ Agenda ▸ Habits only today (org-habit-show-habits-only-for-today). On by default, as in Org; off, habits also show on the later days they are scheduled for. Also on iOS and in Import from Emacs.

Universal (Apple silicon and Intel), macOS 26 or later. Notarized.

item.title: orgstar 0.3.1
item.description:
• The agenda sorts timed entries by time before habits: timed habits go among the timed entries, and the now line and calendar events are placed by start time.
  • iOS: the string catalog is compiled in a build phase, so the German strings are complete.

Universal (Apple silicon and Intel), macOS 26 or later. Notarized.

item.title: orgstar 0.3.0
item.description:
Updates from the app, windows and panes, a watch app, and the rest of Org's agenda, clocking, capture and table options.

  • Updates. orgstar ▸ Check for Updates…, and a daily automatic check that the app asks about on its second launch.
  • Windows and panes. Split Pane Below and Right (C-x 2, C-x 3), Close Pane, Close Other Panes, Next Pane, and New Window (C-x 5 2) for a second window of panes.
  • Agenda. Reminders from the Reminders app; Add to Calendar… and Edit Event… for calendar events; block agendas, per-view sorting, prefix format and skip conditions in views.toml; a Stuck Projects view; the time grid and now line; org-agenda-sorting-strategy; state changes in log mode; org-agenda-todo-ignore-*, org-agenda-start-on-weekday, org-deadline-warning-days and org-agenda-files; holidays in diary sexps.
  • Editor. Incremental search (C-s, C-r); relative and visual line numbers; auto-fill mode; LaTeX previews; remote inline images and images for attachment: links; Insert Drawer, Copy to Refile Target, Go to Refile Target, drag element, bullet cycling; configurable structure templates; coderef and regexp links; org-archive-location, refile targets, tag inheritance settings and org-tag-alist.
  • Capture. regexp targets, template groups, time-prompt, tree-type groupings, Refile… after capture, and the %(…) and %[file] escapes.
  • Clocking. Clocks started or stopped in Emacs or on another device are followed; rounding, a state switch on clock-in, clock out when done, and a notification when the clock passes the Effort; org-clock-into-drawer and CLOCK_INTO_DRAWER; clock tables over other files with :match and :step; the clock report reads open buffers.
  • Tables. table.el tables edited in place; formula iteration and automatic recalculation; #+PLOT with gnuplot or Swift Charts.
  • Code blocks. Ruby, Node and R sessions; :var for Ruby, JavaScript, R and awk; :prologue and :epilogue for interpreted languages.
  • Column view. Values are edited in the sheet; @min, @max and @mean; columnview blocks from file: and ID sources, with :match.
  • Export. Word (.docx), iCalendar, and publishing projects.
  • More of Org. org-attach, org-crypt, radio lists and org-timer, org-track-ordered-property-with-tag, and backlinks and daily notes as in org-roam.
  • Doom. zz, zt and zb, number increment, replace state, q:.
  • Mac. Today, Up Next and Habits widgets for the desktop and Notification Center. German localization.
  • iPhone, iPad and Apple Watch. A watchOS app with today's agenda, the clock and dictated capture; iPad multi-window; keymap.toml and the Doom preset with a hardware keyboard; the board, bulk agenda actions, column view, backlinks, refile from the editor, Word export, table CSV and TSV import and export, and highlighted code in the block editor.

Universal (Apple silicon and Intel), macOS 26 or later. Notarized.
